publications.title: Mono-Hydra++: Real-Time Monocular Scene Graph Construction with Multi-Task Learning for 3D Indoor Mapping
publications.venue: ISPRS Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing
publications.statusLabel: Under review at ISPRS Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing
publications.rightsReason: Under review at an Elsevier journal. The author preprint is on arXiv and is linked here; no version is hosted on this site.
publications.claim: A single camera and an IMU build a hierarchical metric-semantic 3D scene graph of an indoor building in real time, and the map is accurate to 0.08 m.
publications.context: Metric-semantic mapping systems that produce usable scene graphs have almost always assumed RGB-D or LiDAR input, because reliable geometry is the hard part and depth sensors supply it directly. That assumption rules out the platforms where mapping is most useful, since payload and power are what limit small drones. Mono-Hydra++ removes the depth sensor and closes the loop between perception and state estimation instead.
publications.contribution: Predicted sparse depth is fed back into the VIO as metric anchor factors, semantic masks exclude dynamic and unreliable regions from the estimator, and the estimated poses align the dense predictions in time. Each direction of that loop is ablated separately. The components are measured inside the running system, so the comparison does not isolate what any single one contributes on its own.

headline.what: mesh mean error, ITC building 2nd floor
global semantic mesh mIoU on evaluated ScanNet scenes
headline.conditions: fixed mapping backend, RGB plus IMU

limitations: Map quality is multi-objective and the improvements do not move together. On uHumans2 Apartment, adding depth and semantic components raises node F1 from 0.432 to 0.596 while making ATE worse, from 0.068 m to 0.075 m.
On uHumans2 Office the best ATE (1.125 m, K=3) and the best node F1 (0.452, K=1) come from different configurations, so no single setting is best on every axis.
The temporal alignment effect is non-monotonic in window length. Longer is not better.
Evaluation is indoor throughout. Nothing here supports a claim about outdoor or large-scale environments.
publications.hardware: RTX 4080 Super for the full system. Jetson Orin NX 16GB for the exported perception model only.

publications.title: M2H-MX: Multi-Task Semantic and Geometric Perception for Real-Time Monocular 3D Scene Graph Construction
publications.alternateTitle: M2H-MX: Multi-Task Dense Visual Perception for Real-Time Monocular Spatial Understanding
publications.alternateTitleNote: Title used by the arXiv preprint. Recorded so that a search for either phrase resolves here.
publications.venue: IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA) 2026, SRRA Workshop, Vienna
publications.rightsReason: An arXiv preprint exists and could be hosted, but the site hosts no PDFs at all, so this links to arXiv for consistency.
publications.claim: Better per-frame depth and semantics measurably improve the map and the trajectory, not just the benchmark score.
publications.context: Dense prediction papers usually stop at per-frame metrics, which leaves open whether a better model actually produces a better map. M2H-MX is evaluated twice: once as a benchmark predictor, and once as the perception front end inside a running monocular SLAM pipeline that is otherwise unchanged.
publications.contribution: A DINOv3 backbone with LoRA adaptation, a register-gated Mamba decoder, and directed cross-task refinement between depth and semantics. In the ablation, replacing DINOv3 with DINOv2-L costs 8.81 mIoU, while removing the cross-task mixer and the spatial attention costs 2.07. Most of the gain therefore comes from the backbone features rather than from the new decoder blocks.

headline.conditions: M2H-MX-L, RTX 4080 Super. This is +4.06 mIoU points and 9.4 % lower RMSE than M2H.

headline.what: average ATE on selected ScanNet sequences
headline.conditions: Mono-Hydra stack with M2H-MX, monocular. Down from 17.59 cm for monocular Go-SLAM, a 60.7 % reduction. RGB-D baselines in the same table sit at 7.02 to 7.15 cm.

limitations: M2H-MX-L with 4 heads is 353.53 M parameters and 491.91 GFLOPs, which is large for a perception front end.
The gain comes mostly from backbone quality rather than from the proposed decoder blocks.
The ScanNet comparison uses selected sequences, not the full benchmark.
Monocular ATE is close to the RGB-D baselines but does not beat the best of them.
datasets: ScanNet (ScanNet25k subset for the deployed model)
publications.hardware: RTX 4080 Super, 25 to 30 Hz asynchronous perception-to-mapping loop at 640x480.

publications.title: M2H: Multi-Task Learning with Efficient Window-Based Cross-Task Attention for Monocular Spatial Perception
publications.venue: IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS) 2025

identifiers.doiNote: Gap G1. IEEE Xplore DOI not yet recorded.

publications.rightsReason: IEEE copyright. Only an accepted manuscript could be hosted, and the copy held locally is watermarked for review, so nothing is hosted. Links to arXiv and, once recorded, the Xplore DOI.
publications.claim: Four dense prediction tasks share one small model and make each other better, fast enough to sit inside a mapping loop.
publications.context: Mono-Hydra ran an independent depth network and an independent semantic network side by side. That duplicates compute and produces two representations that do not agree with each other. M2H replaces both with one multi-task model in which depth, semantics, surface normals, and edges exchange information through window-based cross-task attention.
publications.contribution: A window-based cross-task attention module that lets tasks exchange structured features while keeping task-specific detail, on a DINOv2-small backbone. In the ablation both the local attention and the global fusion module matter: removing either degrades every task.

headline.conditions: RTX 3080 laptop. Best prior compared: SwinMTL 58.14 mIoU, MTMamba++ 0.4818 RMSE.

headline.what: ITC building 2nd floor mesh mean error, in the Mono-Hydra loop
headline.conditions: 224x224, RTX 3080 laptop. The Mono-Hydra baseline with separate networks reached 0.19 m at 15 fps.
52.31 against 46.66, Table II. Depth RMSE 3.19 against ScaleDepth-NK at 4.825.

limitations: M2H is 81 M parameters and 488 GFLOPs. The parameter count is moderate but the GFLOP count is high.
M2H-small is far cheaper at 33.7 M parameters and 59 GFLOPs, and gives up 3.49 mIoU (58.05 against 61.54).
Boundary detection on NYUDv2 is the one task where the small variant falls behind prior work, at 74.44 odsF.
publications.hardware: Trained on A40. Tested on RTX 3080 laptop, 30 fps.

publications.venue: ISPRS Annals of the Photogrammetry, Remote Sensing and Spatial Information Sciences, volume 1, pages 439 to 445

identifiers.doiNote: Gap G1. ISPRS Annals DOI not yet recorded.

publications.rightsReason: ISPRS Annals is open access, so the published version could be hosted, but the site hosts no PDFs. Links to arXiv and, once recorded, the ISPRS DOI.
publications.claim: A monocular camera and an IMU can build a layered 3D scene graph while the robot is still moving, which the field had only done with depth sensors or LiDAR.
publications.context: Scene graphs represent an environment as a layered graph running from mesh geometry up through objects, places, rooms, and buildings. Systems that build them in real time, Hydra and Kimera and S-Graphs+, all assumed RGB-D or 3D LiDAR input. Removing the depth sensor was largely unexplored, and it is exactly what small aerial platforms need.
publications.contribution: Learned depth and learned semantics feed a robocentric square-root visual-inertial odometry front end, and the resulting semantic mesh drives the Hydra scene graph layers. The contribution is the system rather than any single network. It was the first demonstration of this construction from a monocular camera and an IMU.

headline.what: mesh mean error on the ITC building 2nd and 3rd floors, against a LiDAR backpack point cloud
headline.conditions: DistDepth front end, 848x480, RTX 3080 laptop. The Lite-Mono front end was roughly twice as bad, at 0.39 m and 0.36 m.

headline.what: mesh mean error against Hydra on uHumans2
headline.conditions: Three synthetic scenes, DistDepth 0.05 to 0.28 m, Lite-Mono 0.03 to 0.23 m with higher variance

limitations: The semantic quality of the generated 3D semantic mesh was never quantified, so no accuracy measure for it exists.
Hierarchical loop closure, room detection, and temporal consistency of the mesh are all named as unsolved.
The abstract rounds the mapping result to sub-20 cm, though the 3rd floor measured 0.21 m.
Deployment on embedded hardware needed further network optimisation, which the later work addressed.
publications.hardware: Fine-tuning on TITAN Xp 12GB. System on Alienware m17 laptop, RTX 3080 8GB.

entries.title: Evolution of SLAM: Toward the Robust-Perception of Autonomy
entries.summary: A survey of how SLAM developed from filtering approaches through graph optimisation towards learned components.
entries.abstract: Simultaneous localisation and mapping (SLAM) is the problem of autonomous robots to construct or update a map of an undetermined unstructured environment while simultaneously estimate the pose in it. The current trend towards self-driving vehicles has influenced the development of robust SLAM techniques over the last 30 years. This problem is addressed by using a standard sensor or a sensor array (Ultrasonic sensor, LIDAR, Camera, Kinect RGB-D) with sensor fusion techniques to achieve the perception step. Sensing method is determined by considering the specifications of the environment to extract the features. Then the usage of classical Filter-based approaches, the global optimisation approach which is a popular method for visual-based SLAM and convolutional neural network-based methods such as deep learning-based SLAM are discussed whereas considering how to overcome the localisation and mapping issues. The robustness and scalability in long-term autonomy, performance and other new directions in the algorithms compared with each other to sort out. This paper is looking at the published previous work with a judgemental perspective from sensors to algorithm development while discussing open challenges and new research frontiers.

entries.title: Review of Deep Reinforcement Learning for Autonomous Driving
entries.summary: A survey of deep reinforcement learning applied to autonomous driving, and why results in games transfer badly to the road.
entries.abstract: Since deep neural networks' resurgence, reinforcement learning has gradually strengthened and surpassed humans in many conventional games. However, it is not easy to copy these accomplishments to autonomous driving because state spaces are immensely complicated in the real world and action spaces are continuous and fine control is necessary. Besides, autonomous driving systems must also maintain their functionality regardless of the environment's complexity. The deep reinforcement learning domain (DRL) has become a robust learning framework to handle complex policies in high dimensional surroundings with deep representation learning. This research outlines deep, reinforcement learning algorithms (DRL). It presents a nomenclature of autonomous driving in which DRL techniques have been used, thus discussing important computational issues in evaluating autonomous driving agents in the real environment. Instead, it involves similar but not standard RL techniques, adjoining fields such as emulation of actions, modelling imitation, inverse reinforcement learning. The simulators' role in training agents is addressed, as are the methods for validating, checking and robustness of existing RL solutions.

entries.title: Review on Efficient Strategies for Coordinated Motion and Tracking in Swarm Robotics
entries.summary: A survey of coordinated motion and tracking strategies in swarm robotics.
entries.abstract: Swarm robotics is a creative method of organizing multi-robot structures, consisting of many basic robots influenced by communal insects. The greatest astonishing attribute of swarm robots is their capacity to function together to accomplish a collective objective. This paper addresses the list of current surveys, problems and algorithms that were stimulated in the research of Coordinated Movement in Swarm robotics. Algorithms for swarm robotics movement are contrasted, considering the swarm micro-robots to accomplish aggregation, creation, and clamouring by contrasting the relative computational simulations between the algorithms and simulations used.
